translations.text: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. He was blameless and righteous, feared God, and turned away from evil.
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

He owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very large number of servants. This man was greater than all the people of the East.
His sons would go and hold a feast in each man's house on his day, and they would send for their three sisters and invite them to eat and drink with them.

When the days of feasting had run their course, Job would send for them and consecrate them. Job would rise early in the morning and offer sacrifices corresponding to the number of them all, because Job said, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” Job did this continually.
One day the sons of God came to stand before the Lord, and Satan also came among them to stand before the Lord.
The Lord said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered the Lord, “I have been roaming the earth and walking around on it.”
The Lord said to Satan, “Have you taken notice of my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth, a blameless and upright man who fears God and turns away from evil.”
Satan answered the Lord, “Does Job fear God for nothing?

You have spread your hand protectively over him, his household, his children, and everything he has everywhere. You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have multiplied in the land.
But stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face.”
The Lord said to Satan, “Look, everything he has is handed over to you. Only do not stretch out your hand against him.” Then Satan left the Lord’s presence.
One day Job’s sons and daughters were eating and drinking in their oldest brother’s house.
A messenger came to Job and said to him, “The oxen were pulling the plows, and the female donkeys were grazing beside them.
A band of raiders attacked and carried them off, and the young men were killed with the sword. I alone escaped to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another came and said to him, “The fire of God fell from heaven, swept through the sheep and the shepherds, and burned them up. I alone escaped to tell you.”

While he was still speaking, another came and said to him, “The Chaldeans divided into three bands, attacked the camels, and carried them away. They killed the servants with the sword, and I alone escaped to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another came and said to him, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking in their oldest brother’s house.
“And suddenly a strong wind came from across the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house. It fell on the young people, and they died. I alone escaped to tell you.”
Then Job stood up, tore his robe, shaved his head, and fell to the ground in worship.
He said, “Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I will return. The Lord gave, and the Lord took away. May the Lord's name be blessed.”
In all this Job did not sin or blaspheme against God.
One day the sons of God came to stand before the Lord, and Satan also came among them to stand before the Lord.
The Lord said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered the Lord, “I have been roaming the earth and walking around on it.”

The Lord said to Satan, “Have you taken notice of my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth, a blameless and upright man who fears God and turns away from evil. Even now he holds firmly to his integrity, although you are inciting me against him to destroy him without cause.”
Satan answered the Lord, “Skin for skin! A man will give everything he has in exchange for his life and escape.”
“But stretch out your hand and touch his flesh or his bones, and he will surely curse you to your face.”
The Lord said to Satan, “Look, he is handed over to you. Only spare his life.”
Then Satan left the Lord’s presence and struck Job with painful boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself with, and he sat on the ashes.
His wife said to him, “Are you still holding firmly to your integrity? Curse God and die!”

He said to her, “You have spoken like one of the foolish women. We have accepted good things from God; should we not also accept bad things?” In all this Job did not sin or blaspheme against God with his lips.

Job’s three friends heard about all this calamity that had come upon him. They arranged to come to him, each from his own country: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They agreed to come together to encourage and comfort him.
They looked up from a distance and did not recognize him. They raised their voices and wept, and each tore his robe. They threw dust toward heaven over their heads.
They sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights, and no one said a word, because they saw that his suffering was very severe.
After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day on which he was born.
Job spoke and said:
“May the day on which I was born perish, and the night on which it was said, ‘A boy has been conceived.’
May that day be dark. May God above not seek it out, and may no light shine upon it.
May darkness and the shadows of death cover it. May a cloud settle upon it. May the bitter things of the day terrify it.
May thick darkness cover that night. May that day not be counted among the days of the year, and may it not enter into the numbering of the months.
May that night be barren, and may no song of praise enter it.
May those who curse the day curse it, those who are ready to awaken Leviathan,
May the stars of its dawn grow dark. May they wait for light, but let it have none, and may it not see the rays of dawn.
because it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb and hide trouble from my eyes.
Why did I not die in the womb? Why did I come out of the belly? I should have perished then!
Why did knees rear me, and why did I nurse at breasts?
For then I would now be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest.
With kings and rulers of the earth who built ruins for themselves,
or with rulers who possessed gold and filled their houses with silver.
Or, like a buried miscarriage, I would not have existed, like infants who never saw the light.
There the wicked cease causing trouble, and there those who grew weary in their lives find rest.
Prisoners are at peace together and do not hear the taskmaster’s voice.
The small and the great are there, and the slave is set free from his master.
Why is light given to those who suffer, and life to those whose souls are bitter,
who wait for death, but it does not come, and seek it like treasure,
who rejoice and gather together and exult when they find a grave?
Why is it given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?”
For my sighing comes before my bread, and my groans pour out like water.
For the fear I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has overtaken me.
I was not at ease, nor was I quiet, nor did I rest, and trouble came.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
If one ventures to speak with you, will you grow weary? Yet who can keep words back from you?
Look, you have instructed many and strengthened weak hands.
Your words will not raise up the weak, and you strengthen trembling knees.
For now it has come upon you, and you are weary; it has reached you, and you are dismayed.
Look, your fear itself is your reproach, and your hope is the integrity of your way.
Remember, please: what innocent person has perished, and where has an upright person been put to shame?
As I have seen, those who plow sin and sow trouble will reap it.
By God's breath they perish, and by the wind of his anger they come to an end.
The lion's roar, the voice of the lion cub, and the lions' teeth are broken.
The lion perishes for lack of prey, and the lion cubs are scattered.
A word was brought secretly to me, and my ear received a little of it.
In the stillness, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon people,
Fear and trembling came upon me, and most of my bones shook.
a spirit passed over my face, and the hair of my body stood on end.
It stood still but was unrecognizable. There was no form before my eyes, and I heard a murmur and a voice saying:
Can a human being be more righteous than God, or can a man be purer than his Maker?
Look, he does not trust his servants, and he attributes folly to his angels.
Even those who live in houses of clay, built in the dust, will be brought low before the mist.
From morning to evening they are brought low, so that they will not be established as inhabitants forever, and they will perish.
Look, he takes their inheritance from them, and those who remain among them will die without wisdom.
Call now! Is there anyone who answers you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
For anger kills the fool, and jealousy kills the fool.
I saw a wicked man prospering, but suddenly his dwelling perished.
His children will be far from deliverance; they will be humiliated at the gate, with no one to rescue them.
The hungry will eat what he harvests; it will be poured out for the thirsty, and the thirsty will consume their possessions.
For falsehood does not come out of the dust, nor does wrongdoing sprout from the ground.
For a human being is born for toil, and birds lift their wings.
But I will seek God, and I will lay my case before God.
He does great things without limit and wonders beyond counting.
He gives rain over the earth and sends water over the open places.
He sets the lowly on high, and the humble will be strengthened through deliverance.
He frustrates the plans of the wise, so that their hands cannot carry out their clever schemes.
He catches the wise in their own wisdom and frustrates the counsel of the crafty.
By day they grope as though in darkness; at noon they feel their way as though at night.
He rescues the poor from the sword, from their mouths, and from the hand of the mighty.
Then the poor will have hope, and the wicked man will shut his mouth.
Blessed is the man whom God corrects; let him not reject the discipline of the Almighty.
For he breaks and binds up; he strikes, and his hands heal.
He will rescue you from six troubles, and in the seventh no evil will come near you.
In famine he will rescue you from death, and in battle from the power of the sword.
You will be sheltered from the lash of the tongue, and you will not fear destruction when it comes.
You will laugh at plunder and famine, and you will not fear the wild animals.
For your covenant is with the stones of the field, and the wild animals have submitted to you.
You will know that your tent is secure; you will return to your home and will not go wrong.
You will know that your descendants are many, and your offspring like the grass of the earth.
You will enter the grave peacefully, like a heap of grain brought in at its proper season.
We have investigated this, and this is how it is. Listen to it and know it for yourself.
Then Job answered and said:
If only my anguish could be weighed, together with what has happened to me, on the scales!
For now it is heavier than the sand of the seas; that is why my words are held back.
For the arrows of the Mighty One are in my flesh, and their poison drinks up my spirit; the terror of God has overwhelmed me.
Does a wild donkey bray over grass, or does an ox low over its fodder?
Can tasteless food be eaten without salt, or is there any flavor in the white of an egg?
My soul has grown weary in its struggle, or my insides wail like a drunkard.
If only my request would be granted, and God would give me what I hope for!
May God be willing to crush me, stretch out his hand, and finish me off.
Then I would again have comfort, and again I would be finished off by force without mercy, for I have not been false to the word of the Holy One.
How great is my strength, that I should endure? And what is my end, that I should remain patient?
Is my strength like the strength of stone, or is my flesh bronze?
Look, his help is not within me, and his deliverance has gone far from me.
Whoever withholds peace from his friend abandons the fear of the Most High.
My brothers have been treacherous like streams, like watercourses that pass away.
They were afraid of the ice, and snow piled up over them.
When the sun shines on them, they melt, and in their heat they melt away from their place.
The paths of their courses become tangled; they go up into the wasteland and disappear.
They looked toward the roads of the south and waited for the paths of Sheba.
They were ashamed of what they had trusted; they reached it and were humiliated.
You too have turned against me, for even before you saw the terror, you were afraid.
Did I ever say to you, ‘Give me something,’ or, ‘Pay a bribe on my behalf from your possessions’?
Or, ‘Rescue me from the hands of my oppressor,’ or, ‘Deliver me from the hand of the mighty’?
Teach me, and I will be silent; show me where I have gone wrong.
Why do you reject a true statement? And who among you [?] and rebukes?
Look, you plan to rebuke words, and you scrutinize my speech concerning my spirit.
Look, you lord it over an orphan, and you sell your friend.
Now be persuaded and look: I will speak before you and will not lie.
Please turn back now, and do not be like the unjust. Turn back, then, and be innocent.
Is there injustice on my tongue, or does my mouth not speak the truth?
Look, a person has an allotted time on earth, and his days are like the days of a hired worker.
Like a slave who waits for shade, and like a hired worker who waits to finish his work,
so I have inherited empty months, and nights of misery beyond counting.
When I lie down, I say, “When will I get up?” I count the time until evening; I lie down and toss about until dawn.
My flesh is clothed with worms, and my body with dust. My skin has shriveled and decayed.
My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle and come to an end without hope.
Remember that life is a breath, and my eye will again see good things.
The eye that sees me will not delight in me. Your eyes will be on me, but I will be gone.
As a cloud vanishes and passes away, so someone who goes down to Sheol does not come back up.
He does not return to his house again, and his place no longer knows him.
I too will not restrain my mouth. I will speak in the distress of my spirit and complain in the bitterness of my soul.
Am I the sea or a sea monster, that you set guards over me?
For I said, “You will comfort me, and I will find relief from the distress of my bed.”
But look, you have shaken me with dreams and terrified me with visions.
You have chosen my life over destruction and my bones over death.
I have given up. I will not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are a breath.
What is a human being, that you should destroy him and set your heart on him,
visit him in the morning, and test him at every moment?
How long will you refuse to leave me alone? Will you not let me be until I swallow my saliva?
If I have sinned, what can I do to you, Maker of mankind? Why have you set me against you, so that I have become a burden to myself?
How long will you refuse to forgive my offenses and remove my sins? For now I will lie down in the dust; you will look for me, but I will be gone.
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
“How long will you say these things, with a mighty wind filling your mouth?
Does God pervert judgment, or does the Mighty One pervert justice?”
If your children sinned against him, he sent them away because of their sins.
But if you seek God and plead with the Almighty,
if you are pure and upright, he will now rouse himself on your behalf and make your righteous dwelling secure.
Your beginning will be small, but your latter days will flourish greatly.
Ask, then, about earlier generations, and consider what their ancestors discovered.
For we are only of yesterday and know nothing, and our days on earth are like a shadow.
Look, they will teach you and tell you, and bring forth words from their hearts.
Can rushes flourish in a parched place, or reeds grow where there is no water?
While it is still in bloom and has not been plucked, it withers before any other grass.
Such are the paths of everyone who forgets God, and the hope of the godless will perish.
His confidence will be cut off, and his house is a spider's web.
He will lean on his house, but it will not stand; he will try to hold firm, but it will not endure.
He is like a green plant in the sunlight.
His roots will rest on heaps of stones, and he will look upon a house of stones.
If they uproot him from his place, it will deny him and say to him, 'I have never seen you.'
Look, he examines all his paths, and another will sprout from the dust.
God does not reject the blameless or take evildoers by the hand,
until your mouth is filled with laughter and your lips with praise.
Those who hate you will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.
Then Job answered and said:
I certainly know that this is so, and no human can prevail against God.
For if someone wished to dispute with him, he could not answer him once in a thousand times.
He is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has defied him and come through unharmed?
He moves mountains without anyone knowing and overturns them in his anger.
He shakes the earth from its foundations, and its inhabitants tremble.
He commands the sun, and it does not rise; he seals off the stars.
He alone stretched out the heavens and walked upon the mighty sea.
He made the Pleiades, the Hyades, and Orion, and encircled the south.
He does great things without limit and mighty things beyond counting.
Look, if he passes by me, I do not see him; if he moves around me, I do not perceive him.
Look, if he destroys, who can restrain his hand? Who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
God does not turn back his anger, and many helpers will be humbled beneath him.
How, then, can I answer him and arrange my words before him?
Even if I were in the right, I would not answer; I would plead with my judge.
If I call and he answers me, I do not believe it until he hears my voice.
For he strikes every part of my head with force and multiplies my wounds without cause.
He does not let my spirit rest, for he has filled me with bitterness and drenched me with afflictions.
If it is a matter of strength, he is mighty; if it is a matter of judgment, who can confront him?
Even if I am in the right, my mouth will condemn me. I am blameless, yet he makes me out to be crooked.
I am blameless, yet I do not know myself. I despise my life.
It is all the same. That is why I said, “He destroys both the righteous and the wicked.”
If his scourge suddenly kills, he mocks the folly of the innocent.
He has given the earth into the hand of the wicked, and the faces of its judges are covered. But who can endure his anger?
My days are swifter than a runner. They have fled without seeing anything good.
They have passed away with the many ships of enemies, like an eagle swooping upon its food.
Amid my bitterness I have forgotten my stories. If I abandon my thoughts or my words, I am distressed.
Even if I rest, I fear every torment, for I know that you will not acquit me.
Look, if I am condemned, why do you make me vanish like a breath?
Even if I wash myself with snow water and purify myself by cleansing my hands,
Then you will plunge me into a pit, and my clothes will recoil from me.
For he is not a man like me, so that I could answer him and we could go to court together.
If only there were an arbitrator between us who could place his hand over the mouths of us both!
Let him remove his rod from me, and let his terror no longer shake me.
Then I would speak without fearing him, for I have not been against him.
My soul is weary of my life. I have pondered my thoughts, and I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
I will say to God, “Do not condemn me. Tell me why you are bringing me to judgment.”
Is it not enough for you to oppress and despise the work of your hands, and to look favorably on the plans of the wicked?
Are your eyes like human eyes, or do you see as a human being sees?
Are your days like human days, or your years like the days of a man,
that you investigate my guilt and my sins?
You know that I am innocent, and that no one can escape from your hands.
Your hands labored over me and made me, and afterward you want to condemn me and destroy me.
Remember that you made me like clay, and you are turning me back to dust.
You nourished me like milk and curdled me like cheese.
You clothed me with skin and flesh, and strengthened me with sinews and bones.
You granted me life and peace, and my spirit kept your commandments.
Yet you hid these things in your heart; I knew that this was in your mind:
if I sinned, you would keep watch over me and would not acquit me of my sins.
If I sinned, woe to me! And if I were righteous, I would not lift my head. I am filled with disgrace and have seen my humiliation.
If I rise up, you hunt me like a lion, and again display your might against me.
You sharpen your weapons against me and increase your anger toward me; you bring successive armies against me.
Why did you bring me out of the womb? I should have perished without any eye seeing me.
Then I would have been as though I had never existed, and they would have carried me from the womb to the grave.
The days of my life are few. Leave me alone, so that I may be at ease and rest a little,
before I go, never to return, to the land of darkness and the shadows of death,
which is bleak as ink and the shadows of death, where the generations have no order, and which shines like ink.
Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
Should a multitude of words go unanswered? Nor is a talkative man vindicated by his statements.
Look, only the dead would remain silent at your words! You speak, and no one restrains you; and if you mock, no one rebukes you.
You say that you have acted rightly and have been pure in your own eyes.
But who could make God give an answer and open his lips to speak with you?
And he would show you wisdom’s secrets, for wisdom has many folds, and you would know that God forgives your sins.
Can you discover God’s depths, or can you reach the limits of the Almighty?
Do you know the height of heaven? Or how can you know the depth of Sheol?
Its measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
If he passes by, imprisons, and gathers an assembly, who can turn him back?
For he himself knows when the time has come; he sees injustice and takes notice.
A pure man gains understanding, and one who is mighty helps others.
If you had set your heart right and stretched out your hands toward him,
if there were injustice in your hands, you would have put it far away and would not have let injustice dwell in your tent.
Then you would lift up your hands and would not fear distress.
Then you would forget your trouble and move on like flowing water.
And shame will arise from the noonday, and darkness will be like morning.
You will be confident because there is hope; you will lie down and rest.
There will be no one to wake you, and many will seek your favor.
The eyes of the wicked will grow dark, and their strength will leave them, along with the hope of their souls.
Then Job answered and said:
Truly, you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!
I too have understanding, just as you do, and I am not inferior to you. Who has things like these?
He became a laughingstock to his friends. He called on God, and God answered him, for he delights in the righteous who are without blemish,
to do away with folly and injustice and to steady a faltering foot.
The tents of robbers grow strong, and those who provoke God are secure, because God is not in their hearts.
But ask the animals, and they will teach you; ask the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
Speak to the earth, and it will teach you; the fish in the sea will tell you.
Who does not know through all these things that the hand of the Lord has made them?
For in his hand are the lives of all living things and the breath of all flesh and humankind.
The ear hears words, and the palate tastes food.
Wisdom is among the aged, and understanding comes with length of days.
With him are wisdom and might; counsel and understanding belong to him.
Look, if he tears down, who can rebuild? If he shuts someone in, who can open the door?
If he rebukes the waters, they dry up; if he sends them out, they overturn the earth.
Strength and wisdom belong to him; might and deliverance belong to him.
He leads kings away bewildered and makes fools of judges.
He brings kings down to the gate and binds belts around their waists.
He leads priests away bewildered and brings the mighty low.
He takes speech away from the trustworthy and removes the discernment of elders.
He pours contempt on rulers and weakens the vigor of the strong.
He reveals deep things out of darkness and brings things into the light from the shadows of death.
He leads nations astray and scatters them; he spreads nations out and destroys them; he spreads peoples out and leaves them.
He makes fools of the leaders of the people of the earth and leads them astray in a trackless wasteland.
They grope in darkness and not in light; they feel their way through darkness and not through light, and he makes them wander like drunkards.
Look, my eye has seen all these things, and my ear has heard and understood.
What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
But I will speak to the Almighty, and I will present my argument to God.
But you are speakers of lies, and you are worthless healers.
If only you would remain completely silent! That would count as wisdom for you.
So listen to my argument, and pay attention to the case presented by my lips.
Are you speaking injustice on God's behalf and speaking deceitfully for him?
Are you showing him favoritism, or are you arguing God's case?
Will it be good for you when he examines you? Or do you contend with him as one contends with any ordinary person?
He will certainly rebuke you. Or are you showing him favoritism?
Fear of him will pursue you, and dread of him will fall upon you.
Remember that your authority is made of dust, and your dwelling stands beside clay.
Be silent and leave me alone, so that I too may speak and tell everything that has happened to me.
Why do I carry my flesh in my teeth, with my life placed in my hands?
Even if he kills me, I wait for him, only because my ways are before him.
He himself will also be my savior, because a [?] does not come before him.
Listen carefully to my words, and I will state my declaration before you.
Look, I too am presenting my case, and I know that I am in the right.
Who is there to dispute with me? For now I will be silent and rest.
But do not deny me two things; then I will not hide from your presence.
Do not withdraw your hand from me, and do not let your terror shake me.
Call me, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.
How many offenses and sins do I have? Make my offenses and sins known to me.
Why do you turn your face away from me and consider me your enemy?
Do you trample a dry, falling leaf and pursue dry stubble?
For you have written out punishment against me, and you bring up against me the sins of my youth.
You have put my feet in the stocks and watched all my ways, and you watch where I plant my feet.
And he is like a rotten thing wasting away, like a garment eaten by moths.
Such is a human being born of a woman: his days are few, and he endures turmoil.
He comes forth like a flower, dries up and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not remain.
Even on someone like this you have opened your eyes, and you bring him into judgment with you.
Who can bring something clean out of something unclean? Not even one.
If his days are determined and the number of his months is decreed, you have established a limit that he cannot pass.
Let him rest until he has run through his days like a hired worker.
For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it sprouts again, and its branches do not die away.
Even if its root grows old in the earth and its stump dies in the dust,
at the scent of water it will sprout and produce leaves like a young plant.
But a man dies and decays; a human being wastes away and is no more.
Water disappears from the sea, and a river becomes parched and dries up.
And a man who lies down does not rise. Until the heavens wear out, they will not awaken or stir from their sleep.
Who could bring it about that you would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until your anger passes, and then appoint a time for me and remember me?
If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of his youth he waits until his old age comes.
If you call me, I will answer you; give thought to the work of your hands.
For now, do not count my steps or hold my sins against me.
Seal my offenses in a bag, and remove my sins from me.
Surely a mighty mountain falls, or a rock is moved from its place.
Water wears away stone, or washes away the soil of the earth; you have destroyed a person's hope.
You overpower him forever, and he departs; you send him away with shame on his face.
If his children increase, he does not know; if they decrease, he is unaware of them.
But his flesh suffers pain, and his soul mourns over him.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Should someone wise in spirit answer with knowledge and fill his belly with anger?
Should he argue with useless words and with speech that brings no benefit?
You too are doing away with reverence and multiplying words before God.
For your mouth teaches sins, and you favor the language of deceit.
Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips testify against you before me.
Were you born before mankind, or were you conceived before the hills?
Have you listened in the Lord's secret council, and has wisdom been revealed to you?
What do you know that we do not know? Or what do you understand that is not known to us?
Look, among us are gray-haired men and elders, including those older in days than your father.
Keep God's threats away from you, and speak gently to yourself.
Why has your heart become proud, and why do your eyes flash?
For you raise your spirit against God and pour words out of your mouth.
What is a human being, that he should be pure? Or how can one born of a woman be righteous?
Look, he does not trust his holy ones, and the heavens are not pure before him.
Even though a man is despised and rejected, he drinks wrongdoing like water.
I will tell you; listen to me, and I will recount what I have seen.
What the wise have declared and have not concealed from their fathers.
To them alone the land was given, and no foreigner passed among them.
All his days the wicked man exalts himself, and a fixed number of years is reserved for the mighty man.
The sound of terror is in his ears, and in peacetime a plunderer will come upon him.
He does not believe that he will return from darkness; he looks toward the sword.
He flees to the battle of judgment, and wherever he is, he knows that the day of darkness is ready at hand.
Distress will terrify him, and anguish will overwhelm him, like a king prepared for battle.
Because he raised his hand against God and defied the Almighty.
He rushed at him with his neck held high and stiff, with many ranks of shields.
He covered his face with his fat and made a mound above the [?].
He settled ruined towns that were uninhabited and prepared for battle.
He will not last, nor will his strength endure, nor will he cast words upon the earth.
They will not escape from darkness. The flame will dry up his branches; he will be swept away by the breath of his mouth.
He should not trust deceptive falsehood, because his reward has become emptiness.
He will wither before his time, and his hands will not be found.
He will tear off his unripe grapes like a vine and shed his blossoms like an olive tree.
For the assembly of the godless will become a ruin and a desolation, and fire will consume the tent of the wicked.
They conceived injustice and gave birth to trouble, and their bellies are full of deceit.
Job answered and said:
I have heard many things like these, and you all offer me false comfort.
Do not distress my spirit with words. Even if you speak to me, I will not answer.
I too could speak as you do. If only you were in my place! I would put you to the test with words and shake my head at you.
I would examine you by your words, and I would not withhold the speech of my lips from you.
For if I speak, my pain does not go away; and if I remain silent, who will bring me relief?
For now he has wearied me and has kept all my testimony.
He made me stand up, and I became a witness. My falsehood rose up against me, and I spoke before him.
His anger broke me and tore me apart, and he gnashed his teeth at me. My enemies together fixed their eyes on me.
They opened their mouths against me in scorn, struck my cheeks together, and were filled with fury against me.
He handed me over to an unjust angel and delivered me into the hand of the wicked.
I was at ease, but he shattered me. He seized me by the neck and scattered me. He set me up as his target.
His arrows multiplied against me. He shot into my kidneys without pity and poured my bile onto the ground.
He broke through me, breach after breach, and rushed against me as against a warrior.
I fastened sackcloth over my skin and sprinkled dust on my head.
My face is clouded by weeping, and my eyes by the shadow of death.
Even though there is no wrongdoing in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
Earth, do not cover my blood, and let there be no place for my cries.
And now, look: my witnesses are in heaven, and those who know me are on high.
My brothers and my friends, my eye pours out tears to God.
If only a human being could argue with God as a man does with his friend.
For his numbered years are coming, and he goes down a road from which there is no return.
My spirit is shattered, and my days have been extinguished. Prepare a grave for me.
For there is no falsehood in me, and my spirit spends the night in their bitterness.
Please keep my pledge with you. Who is there to clasp my hand?
Because you have hidden their hearts from understanding, therefore they will be exalted in division.
A friend will exalt himself over his friend, and the eyes of their children will grow dark.
I will establish the rule of the nations, and I will be a covering over their faces.
My eye aches from anger, and all my thoughts are like shadows.
The upright will be astonished at this, and the innocent will rise up against the guilty.
The righteous will hold to his way and persevere, and the one whose hands are clean will grow stronger.
But look, all of you have returned, turned around, and come to me, yet I have not found anyone wise among you.
They make days pass, frustrate plans, and destroy the hearts of peoples.
You turn night into day and bring light near before darkness.
If I wait for Sheol, it is my home, and I have spread my bed in darkness.
I called decay, “You are my father,” and the worm, “My mother and my sister.”
Where, then, are my hope and my confidence? Who can find my hope?
You will go down by force to Sheol, and together they will descend to the dust.
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
“How long will you oppose these words? Think carefully, and afterward we will speak.
Why are we regarded as cattle and considered unclean in your eyes?
He kills himself in his anger! Will the earth be abandoned for your sake, or a mountain moved from its place?
The lamp of the wicked will also go out, and the flame of his fire will grow dim.
The light will grow dark in their tents, and his lamp above him will go out.
His steps will falter because of his pains, and his own counsel will bring him down.
For he has stretched his foot into a trap and walked over a net.
A snare has caught his heel; the thirsty will overpower him.
His rope is hidden in the ground, and his trap is laid along the paths.
Ranks of terrors surround him and drive his feet in every direction.
Hunger will be his pain, and destruction is prepared for his offspring.
His skin will be devoured by force, and his firstborn by the might of the dead.
His confidence will be cut off from his tent, and the terrors of a king will drive him away.
They will dwell in his tent, since no one is there; sulfur will be scattered over his dwelling.
His roots below will dry up, and his branch above will fall off.
His memory will perish from the earth, and he will have no name anywhere in the world.
They will thrust him from light into darkness and drive him out of the world.
He has neither name nor remembrance among the people, and he will have no survivor in his dwelling.
Those who come afterward will be appalled at his days, and the hair of those who came before will stand on end.
Surely these are the tents of the unjust, and this is the dwelling of one who does not know God.”
Then Job answered and said:
“How long will you torment my soul and hurt me with words?
Look, you have reproached me ten times, and you are not ashamed to grieve me.
Even if I have truly gone astray, my error remains with me.
And if you have indeed exalted yourselves over me, rebuking and insulting me,
know, then, that it is God who has condemned me and spread his net over me.
If I cry out, no one answers me; if I lament, no one takes up my cause.
He has fenced off my paths so that I cannot pass, and he has put darkness over my trails.
He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.
He has uprooted me on every side, and I am gone; he has pulled up my hope like a tree.
His anger has grown fierce against me, and he considers me his enemy.
His messengers came against me together, made their way against me, and camped around my tent.
My brothers have gone far away from me, and my acquaintances have passed me by.
My relatives have cut themselves off from me, and my acquaintances have forgotten me.
Those staying in my house and my maidservants consider me a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their eyes.
I called my servant, but he did not answer me. I begged him with the words of my own mouth and pleaded with him.
I became a stranger to my wife, and I begged my own son for mercy.
Even little children despise me; when I stand up, they speak against me.
All those who gave me counsel despised me, and even my friends turned against me.
My skin and flesh cling to my bones, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, you my friends, because the hand of God has touched me.
Why do you too persecute me like God? Why are you not satisfied with my flesh?
If only someone would have my words written down and recorded in a book,
and have them engraved on rock forever with an iron pen and a lead stylus!
But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end he will appear on the earth.
And around my skin these things were wrapped [?], and around my flesh.
If my eyes, which see the light, should see God [?]. For my kidneys have completely wasted away because of my condition.
For you say, “Why are we persecuting him?” For he has found a good argument against me.
Save yourselves from the sword, because wrath against sins is a sword, so that you may know there is judgment.
Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
Because of my conduct they answered me, and for my sake they waited for me.
I hear correction that rebukes me, and the spirit of my understanding will answer me.
You have known this from long ago, since Adam was created on earth: who made human beings on earth?
For the praise of the wicked comes from among themselves, and the joy of the godless lasts only a short time.
Even if his height rises to heaven and his head reaches the clouds.
Like a whirlwind he will perish forever. Those who saw him will say, “Where is he?”
Like a dream he will fly away and not be found; he will vanish like a vision of the night.
The eye that saw him will never see him again, and they will no longer look upon his place.
His sons will be crushed by poverty, and his hands will reach out toward his offspring.
His bones are full of marrow, and they will lie with him on the ground.
If his wickedness tastes sweet in his mouth, and he hides deceit under his tongue,
he cherishes it and does not let it go, and keeps it within his darkness.
His food will turn in his bowels, and a serpent’s gall will be within him.
He will bring back from his belly the food he swallowed, and God will destroy him.
He will suck the venom of a cobra, and the tongue of an asp will kill him.
He will not see the branching rivers and streams of honey and [?].
He will give back what he labored for and will not swallow it; he will not enjoy the wealth received in exchange.
For he resolved to abandon the poor, and a house acquired by robbery will not be built.
For he did not recognize the judgment within his belly, and he will not escape with the things he desires.
None of his offspring escapes; therefore his prosperity will not last.
He will be repaid with the measure he measured out, and every hand of the unjust will come against him.
His belly will be doomed to destruction. He will unleash his fierce anger against him and rain it down on him in his assault.
The one who flees from iron armor will be pierced by a bronze bow.
It will be drawn out and emerge from his body, and the membrane of his gallbladder will be torn. Suffering will constantly be upon him.
All darkness is stored up for his offspring. A fire that has not been fanned will consume him, and whatever remains in his tent will wither.
The heavens will reveal his sins, and the earth will take vengeance on him.
The foundations of his house will be exposed, and he will be dragged away on the day of wrath.
This is the wicked person’s portion from God, and the inheritance of his words from on high.
Job answered and said:
Listen carefully to my words, and let there be understanding among you.
Bear with me while I speak, and after my words, mock me.
Do I address my words to a human being? Why is my spirit distressed?
Turn toward me and be astonished; put your hands over your mouths.
For when I remember, I am shaken, and trembling seizes my flesh.
Why do the wicked live on and grow old, mighty in strength?
Their offspring are established before them, and their children are before their eyes.
Their houses are peaceful, free from fear, and God's rod is not upon them.
Their bull mates and does not bellow; their cow gives birth and does not miscarry.
They let their children loose like a flock, and their little ones dance.
They take up tambourines and lyres and rejoice at the sound of music.
They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in a moment.
They say to God, 'Leave us alone! We do not want to know your ways.'
They say, 'Who is God, that we should serve him? What do we gain by making requests of him?'
Look, their prosperity is not in their own hands, and the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
How often is the lamp of the wicked extinguished, and disaster comes upon them? How often does his anger deal out destruction?
And how often do they become like straw before the wind, like chaff carried away by a whirlwind?
God stores up a man's guilt for his children. Let him repay the man himself, so that he may know it.
Let his own eyes see his destruction, and let him drink from God's wrath.
What concern does he have for his household after him? And will the number of his months be preserved for his children?
Are you teaching God knowledge, when he judges those on high?
For one may die in the fullness of his strength, having been secure and at ease,
with his sides full of fat and his bones full of marrow.
Another dies bitter in spirit, never having enjoyed good things.
Together they lie on the earth, and worms cover them.
Look, I know your thoughts and the plans you are devising against me.
For you said, “Where is the righteous man’s house, and where is the campsite of the wicked?”
For you have not asked those who travel the roads, and you have not recognized their signs.
For the wicked man is reserved for the day of destruction and remembered for the day of wrath.
Who shows him his way, and who repays him for what he has done?
He goes to the grave and is kept under watch at the burial mound.
The clods of the valley swallow him. Everyone is drawn along after him, and those before him are beyond counting.
How can you comfort me with empty words? The replies to his words remain before me.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
“Do you speak with God, O man, as though you had become his equal in wisdom?
And what benefit is there in your making your ways perfect? Is it out of fear of you
that he would rebuke you and enter into judgment with you?
Look, your wickedness is great, and there is no end to your sins.
For you took pledges from your brothers without cause and stripped the naked of their clothing.
You gave the weary no water to drink, and you withheld bread from the hungry.
A man sows a field for himself, but a powerful master takes it away from him.
You sent the widow away empty-handed and weakened the orphan’s arm.
That is why snares surround you and sudden terror shakes you.
The darkness is [?]; you did not see it, and a flood of water will cover you.
Look, God has raised the heavens; see how high the tops of the stars have been raised.
And you say, ‘What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?
For clouds conceal him, and [?] does not see; he walks on the vault of heaven.’
Have you kept to the ancient path that deceitful people trod before their time?
They were stopped at the river crossing, and they did not remember the one who established their foundations.
They say to God, ‘Leave us! What does God do for us?’
He filled their houses with good things, and the counsel of the wicked was far removed from them.
The righteous will see and rejoice, and the innocent will mock them.
But they will be brought low from their stubbornness, and fire will consume what remains of them.”
Come to terms with him, then, and repay them from your good harvests.
Receive instruction from his mouth, and he will place his words in your heart.
If you return to God, you will be built up, and if you remove wrongdoing from your tent,
you will gather silver like dust, and gold from Ophir like sand from a stream.
God will be your help, and you will have silver [?].
And you will lift your face toward God.
You will pray before him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
You will declare something, and he will establish it for you, and light will shine on your paths.
For he says that the one who is humbled will be raised up, and the one whose eyes are lowered will be saved.
The innocent person will escape wherever he is; he will escape through the purity of his hands.
Then Job answered and said:
Even today my complaint is bitter, and his hand weighs heavily upon my groaning.
Who, then, would make it possible for me to reach his seat?
I would set out my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
Then I would know what he would answer me, and I would understand what he would say to me.
Would he judge me with great power? Or would he lay terror upon me?
There I would argue my case uprightly with him; I would be vindicated and escape judgment.
If he goes before me, I do not know it, and from behind him I cannot perceive him.
I searched to my left, but he did not appear to me; I turned to my right, but I did not see him.
He knows my way and my conduct; he tested me like gold, and I came out.
My feet stood firm in his paths; I kept his ways.
I did not despise the commands of his lips, and I did not depart from his will. I kept the words of his mouth.
And he is in one of these; what will he answer me? What he himself desired, he did.
Yet he has carried out his decree, and he has many such things with him.
Therefore I was afraid before him; I considered this and trembled before him.
For God has shaken my heart, and my head has been shaken.
For I was not silenced before the darkness or before the covering of gloom.
Why were the wrongdoers not hidden from God? They were known, yet they did not see their days.
They moved the boundary and drove away the flock.
They drove away the orphan’s donkey and took the widow’s ox as a pledge.
The wretched hid from the road, and the humble of the land hid together.
Like wild donkeys in the wilderness, they rise early for food, for bread for their young.
They reap in a hot field that is not theirs, and glean the vineyards of the wicked.
The naked man spends the night without clothing, with no covering against the cold.
They are drenched by the mountain downpours, and embrace the rocks for lack of shelter.
They snatch away from the orphans’ plunder and inflict injuries on the poor.
They went about naked, without clothing, and carried bread while hungry.
At meals they bend down and go hungry while carrying a seah and a measure; at times they go hungry at their meals. They tread winepresses and go thirsty.
From within the town the dead groan, and the soul of the slain cries out, but God does not accept their prayer.
They were among those who [?] the light; they did not know its ways or walk in its paths.
At daylight the murderer rises and kills the poor and the wretched; at night he becomes like a thief.
The eyes of adulterers wait for darkness, saying, “No eye will see me,” and he hides his face in the darkness.
He breaks into houses in the darkness and seals them up during the day so that they do not see the light.
Therefore they sought the shadow of death for themselves and found it, and the shadows of death terrified them.
He is swift upon the surface of the water; their portion in the land, along the vineyard path, will be cursed.
Drought and heat snatch away the snow water; they sinned in Sheol.
They were forgotten by the womb; the worm found them sweet. The dead will no longer be remembered, and the wrongdoer will be broken like a tree.
The unfortunate barren woman will not give birth; they showed no kindness to the widow.
The strong man’s property will endure through his strength, but he will not trust in the vision.
He will dwell quietly and feel secure, and his eyes will be lifted toward their ways.
A little while, and they are gone. They will be brought low, and all who provoke anger will perish. Like heads of grain, they will dry up and crumble.
If this is not so, let his anger prove me a liar, and let my words be weighed before God.
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
Dominion and fear belong to him; he makes peace in his heights.
His army cannot be counted, and on whom does his light not shine?
How can a human being be righteous before God, or how can someone born of a woman be pure?
Look, even the moon cannot be pure, and the stars are not pure before him.
Indeed, a human being is a maggot, and a mortal is a worm.
Then Job answered and said:
Why do you help someone who has no strength, and rescue an arm that has no might?
What counsel you have given to someone without wisdom! What great learning you have made known!
To whom have you declared these words, and whose breath has come out of you?
Look, the mighty will be killed, and they will be drawn out of the waters.
Sheol is naked before him, and there is no covering for Abaddon.
He stretches out the north from the wasteland and hangs the earth on nothing.
He binds up the waters in his clouds, and the cloud is not torn open beneath them.
He closes off the face of the covering and spreads a cloud above it.
He has marked a circle on the surface of the waters, until light and darkness come to an end.
The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.
By his power he rebukes the sea, and by his wisdom he strikes down many.
By his spirit he directs the heavens, and his hand killed the fleeing serpent.
Look, all these are only part of his ways. What evil word has been heard about him? And who can understand the greatness of his might?
Job continued his discourse and said:
As God lives, who has delayed my judgment, and the Almighty, who has made my life bitter,
For all of it is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils.
my lips will not speak injustice, nor will my tongue speak deceit.
Far be it from me! Until I die, my integrity will not depart from me.
I will hold firmly to my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart has not reproached me throughout my days.
May my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who hates me like the unjust.
What hope does the godless person who has acquired possessions have when God takes away his life?
For God will not listen to his prayer when trouble comes upon him.
But if he trusts in the Mighty One and calls upon God at all times, God will answer him and listen to him.
But you—I hand you over into God's hand, for your deeds are not hidden from him.
Look, all of you have seen it. Why, then, do you boast so vainly?
Look, this is the wicked person's portion from God, and the inheritance that evildoers will receive from the Mighty One.
Even if their sons become numerous, they are destined for the sword, and their offspring will not have enough bread.
Those who remain will be buried in death, and their widows will not weep.
Even if they heap up silver like dust and prepare clothing like clay,
they will prepare it, but the righteous person will wear it and divide their silver.
For he built his house like a spider's, and made his shelter like a temporary hut.
For the rich man will lie down and will not rise again; he opens his eyes, and he is no more.
Distress will overtake him like water, and at night the wind will carry him away like a flying [?].
He will depart, and they will drive him from his place.
It will cast him away without mercy, and he will flee desperately from his hand.
He will clap his hand at them and hiss at them from his place.
For silver has a source, and there is a place where gold is refined.
Iron is smelted from the earth, and copper is smelted from stones.
He sets a limit to darkness, and he knows every boundary—the stone of darkness and the shadow of death.
They inherited a fissure from a foreign people; they were forgotten by passing feet and dwindled away from other people.
They laid bare the earth from which food comes, and underneath it is turned over as by fire.
Its stones are a source of sapphires, and gold dust is in its paths.
No bird has known it, and the kite's eye has not seen it.
Wild animals have not trodden it, nor has a lion passed over it.
He reached out his hand against the flint rock and overturned mountains at their roots.
By his strength he divided rivers, and his eye saw every precious thing.
He restrained the force of the rivers, and light came out of concealment.
But where can wisdom be found, and where is the place of understanding?
No one knows its treasure, and it is found nowhere except in the land of the living.
The deep says, “It was not in me,” and the sea says, “It is not with me.”
Gold cannot be given in exchange for it, nor can silver be counted out as its price.
It cannot be exchanged for the gold of Ophir, beryl, or sapphire.
Gold, glass, and fine pearls cannot compare with it; rings and beads cannot compare with it.
Wisdom is better than precious stones. [?] cannot compare with it, and it cannot be exchanged for emeralds or carbuncles. For wisdom is better than everything, and nothing can compare with it.
The pearls of Cush and topaz stones cannot compare with it.
Where does wisdom come from, and where is the place of understanding?
It is concealed from the eyes of every living creature and hidden from the birds of the sky.
Destruction and Death say, “With our ears we have heard a report of it.”
For God understands its paths, and he knows its place.
For he sees to the ends of everything on earth, and he sees beneath all the heavens.
He made a weight for the wind and established a weight by measure.
He made a law for the rain and a path for the flashes of thunder.
Then he saw it and declared it; he weighed it and also examined it.
He said to humanity, “The fear of God—that is wisdom, and turning away from evil is understanding.”
Job continued his discourse and said:
“Who will make me as I was in earlier months, as in the days when God watched over me?
He placed his fear above my head, spreading his lamp over me, and by his light I walked in darkness.
As I was in the days of my favor, when God sheltered my tent over me,
and when the Mighty One surrounded my youth,
when I went out to the gate and called out, and sat in the marketplace like a wicked man.”
Young men saw me and hid, and old men stood up and marveled at me.
The nobles stopped speaking and put their hands over their mouths.
The voices of rulers were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
For the ear that heard me praised me, and the eye that saw me bore witness for me.
For I rescued the poor from distress, and the orphan who had no helper.
The blessing of the one who was perishing would come upon me, and I made the widow’s heart glad.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me like a robe and a crown of justice.
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the unfortunate, and I investigated cases I did not know.
I broke the fangs of the wicked and pulled the prey out from between his teeth.
And I said, “I will rescue the poor people, and I will reach my end like a reed, and I will multiply my days like the sand of the seas.”
My roots are planted beside water, and dew will remain overnight, and at harvest I will be called.
It was joined to me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.
And if they listened to me and waited and heeded my counsel,
and did not stray from my words, and my speech was pleasing to them.
They waited for me as for rain, and opened their mouths as for the spring rain.
I would laugh at them, but they would not believe, and they would not walk in the light of my face.
I would examine their paths and return, and dwell like a king among his troops, and like a man who comforts mourners.
But now, look, those younger than I am laugh at me—those whose fathers I rejected and would not even rank with the dogs of my flock.
And what use was the strength of their hands to me, since all their vigor had perished?
And it burst upon them by force, like a thief with powerful legs.
To dwell in hollows of earth and stone,
and beneath cliffs and beneath thornbushes.
Foolish sons will be cast down along with wicked sons; there they will be brought low from the earth.
And now I have become their song, and I have become an object of astonishment to them.
They rejected me and kept far from me, and they did not withhold spit from my face.
For they camped behind me and humbled me, and put his bridle in my mouth.
They stood at my right hand and tripped my feet; they obstructed me along the paths of their ways.
They obstructed my paths for no reason and rejoiced over what happened to me, but they will have no help.
They will come like a great breach, and beneath the storm they will be shattered.
For they turned turmoil against me and pursued my paths like the wind, and my deliverance was like a passing cloud.
Now my soul is battered, and the days of my humiliation surround me.
At night my bones weighed heavily on me, and my body found no rest under the great force.
I put on my clothes and girded myself with my tunic.
They likened me to clay, and I became like dust and ashes.
I cry out to you, but you do not answer me. I stood up, and you looked closely at me.
You made me your enemy and hated me with the strength of your hands.
You lifted me up and set me astride the wind; you humbled me and made me suffer.
Now I know that you will bring me back from death to the meeting place of all the living.
Yet may he not stretch out his hand against me; when I cry out to him, may he rescue me.
I wept for the poor during the day, and my soul was distressed for the afflicted.
I waited for good, but evil came. I waited for light, but darkness came.
My insides were in turmoil and did not rest; days of humiliation came upon me.
I walked about mournfully, without warmth. I stood up in the assembly and wept.
I became a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.
My skin has shriveled on me, and my bones are scorched as if by heat.
My harp turned to mourning, and my singing to the sound of weeping.
I made a covenant with my eyes not to gaze at a virgin.
What is the portion from God above, and the inheritance from God on high?
Is it not ruin for the wicked and estrangement for those who do wrong?
He is the one who sees my paths and counts all my steps.
If I have walked with liars, and if my feet have hurried to run deceitfully,
let him weigh me on honest scales, and let God know my integrity.
If my steps have strayed from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, and if anything has clung to me,
but only if I sowed did I then eat, and if I planted, then I raised the crop and gathered it.
And if my heart was enticed by another man's wife, and if I lay in wait at my neighbor's door,
Then let my wife grind grain for others and bake in another place.
For that is a sin, and it is a source of deceit.
It is a fire that consumes to the point of destruction, and let all my crops be uprooted.
If I rejected the case of my male or female servant when they had a dispute with me—
But I said, “What will I do when God rises up? When he calls me to account, what will I answer him?”
For the one who made me in the womb made him, and he formed us in the same womb.
If I withheld from the poor what they wanted, and if I darkened the widow’s eyes;
if I ate my bread alone, and the orphan did not eat any of it—
For pains raised me from my youth, and sighs from my mother’s womb.
If I saw someone perishing for lack of clothing, or a needy person without a covering—
But they were raised on my knees and warmed with the fleece of my sheep.
If I raised my hand against an orphan—but whenever I saw him at the gate, I helped him—
let my shoulder fall from its socket, and let my arm be broken from its joint.
For fear of God shook me, and destruction from him came upon me, and I could not stand because of trembling.
If I made gold my confidence, and if I said to a precious stone, “You are my confidence,” and if I said to fine gold, “You are my hope”;
and if I rejoiced because my possessions were abundant and because my hand had acquired much;
if I saw the light when it was radiant, and the moon when it was lovely;
if my heart went astray and was secretly enticed, and my hand kissed my mouth—
He too sees all my deceitful deeds, if I have lied before God.
And if I rejoiced at the ruin of someone who hated me, and if I was delighted when disaster befell him—
I did not surrender my mouth to sin, nor did I desire any one of these things.
But my friends said, “Who, then, will give us some of his flesh? We have not had our fill.”
I did not make a stranger spend the night in the street, and I opened my door to the traveler.
If I concealed my sins like other people, and if I secretly buried my offenses;
and if I trampled the strength of many—but the multitude of clans broke me, and I did not turn anyone away at the gate, and I did not dwell on the speech of lips. God’s threats humbled me.
Who, then, will give me someone to hear me? If he is God, let him answer me and write the man's case in a book.
Rather, I would carry it on my shoulder and make it a crown for myself.
I would show him the number of my steps and, like a ruler, declare it to him.
If the land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,
if I have consumed its produce without payment, or caused a bitter soul distress,
let dung come up instead of wheat, and thorns instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
These three men stopped trying to condemn Job, because he was righteous in their eyes.
Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram, became angry. His anger burned against Job because he considered himself more righteous than God.
He was also angry with Job's three friends because they could find no answer to give Job and condemn him.
Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were older than he was.
When Elihu saw that these three men could give him no answer, his anger burned.
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, “Because I am younger than you and you are old, I was afraid and trembled at the thought of showing you what I know.
For I said, ‘Age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.’
Truly, there is a spirit in a human being, and the breath of God gives them understanding.
Yet many days do not make people wise, nor do the old necessarily understand justice.
Therefore I say: Listen to me, and I too will show you what I know.
Look, I remained silent before you and your words, and listened until you lost your way; I examined you through your words.
I considered your testimony, and look: none of you has refuted Job or given him an answer.
For you say, ‘We have found wisdom. It is God who strikes him, not a human being.’
He has not spoken against the words, and I will not contend with him using your words.
They fell silent and no longer answered him; words deserted them, and they were silent.
Since they do not speak, since they have stopped and no longer answer him,
I too will give my answer, and I too will show what I know.
For I am full of words, and a spirit has been poured into my belly.
Look, my belly is in pain and cannot open; like a wineskin in the month [?], it is bursting.
I will speak so that I may find relief; I will open my lips and give an answer.
I will show no favoritism to anyone, and I will not be ashamed before anyone.
For I know no shame, and soon my strength would carry me away.
But listen to my words, Job, and pay attention to everything I say.
Look, I have opened my mouth, and my tongue speaks within my mouth.
The speech of my mouth is upright, and the words of my lips are carefully chosen.
The Spirit of God has stirred me, and the breath of God has given me life.
If you can, give me an answer. Prepare yourself and stand before me.
I am like you before God; I too was formed from clay.
Now, fear of me will not shake you, and my pressure on you will not weigh heavily.
But you spoke within my hearing, and I heard the sound of your words.
You said, “I am pure, without guilt. I am righteous, and there are no sins in me. I am free from wrongdoing.
Yet he finds grounds for accusations against me and considers me his enemy.
He puts my feet in the stocks and watches all my paths.”
In this you cannot prove yourself right. I will answer you: God is greater than a human being.
Why have you argued with him, when he does not answer for all his words?
For God speaks once and does not repeat it a second time, and he pays no attention to lips.
In a dream, in a vision of the night, when sleep falls upon a person, while he slumbers on his bed,
then he opens a person's ear and humbles people in their rebellion.
To turn a person away from his deeds, and he rebukes a man's body.
He keeps a person's soul from destruction and his life from perishing.
He rebukes him with pain on his bed, and the mass of his bones grows strong.
His flesh wastes away from fear, and his appetite is not satisfied with bread; he craves food.
His flesh will be consumed by his fear, and the bulk of his bones will not be seen.
His soul draws near to destruction, and his life to death.
If he has an angel who listens to him, one out of a thousand, he will show the person what is right for him.
He will have mercy on him and say, “Rescue him so that he does not go down to destruction,” and he will find deliverance for him.
His flesh will be renewed as it was in his childhood, and he will return to the days of his youth.
He will pray before God, and God will hear him and be pleased with him. He will appear before him in glory, and God will repay the man for his righteousness.
He will speak truthfully to people and say, “I have sinned and truly done wrong, and I have brought myself no benefit.
Rescue my soul from perishing in destruction, so that my soul may see the light.”
God does all these things three times with a person.
He turns his soul back from destruction so that he may see the light of life.
Pay attention, Job, and listen. Be silent, and I will speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me, because I want you to be vindicated.
But if not, listen to me. Be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.
Elihu answered and said:
Listen to my words, you wise people; pay attention to me, you who have knowledge.
For the ear tests words, and the palate tastes food.
Let us choose justice for ourselves and discover among ourselves what is good.
You spoke, Job, and declared yourself innocent, saying, “I have been vindicated, but God has turned my case against me.”
Who has perished without wrongdoing?
What man is like Job, who drinks mockery like water?
He becomes a partner and companion of evildoers, walking with sinful people.
For you said that a man gains nothing when he fears God.
Therefore, you people of understanding, listen to me. Far be it from God to do wrong, and far be it from him to commit sin.
For he repays a person according to his deeds, and a man receives according to his ways.
Truly, God does no wrong, nor does God obstruct the way.
Who gave orders to the earth, and who made the whole world?
If he turns his attention toward him, his spirit and his breath are gathered back to him.
All flesh perishes together, and humanity returns to its dust.
If you have understanding, hear these things and pay attention to the sound of my words.
One who hates justice is not innocent; and if he is innocent, he is condemned unjustly.
Who says of a king, “He has ruled unjustly,” [?] leaders [?] rulers.
He shows no partiality to the great and no partiality to the poor, because they are all the work of his hands.
Suddenly they die, and in the middle of the night they perish and are lost; they acknowledge the Mighty One, not through force.
For his eyes are on all a person's ways, and he sees every step.
There is no darkness or shadow of death where evildoers can hide.
For he does not again require a person to enter into judgment with God.
He has brought harm on countless people and will raise up others together in their place.
Therefore he recognized them by their deeds, and he will overthrow them at night.
Their deeds will be brought low under injustice in a terrible place.
Because they turned away from following him and paid no attention to any of his ways.
The prayer of the poor comes before him, and he hears the cry of the afflicted.
If he forgives, who can condemn? If he turns his face away, who can forgive, whether a nation or an individual?
So that he would not make a [?] and sinful man king over the people.
For God said, “I have forgiven; I do not destroy without sins.”
Teach me yourself if I have done wrong.
I will no longer give you an answer because I have sinned. For you have examined the matter, not I. Say what you know.
People of understanding will speak to me, and a wise man will listen to me.
Job does not speak with knowledge, and his words lack understanding.
Job has certainly been tested to the end, and he is not counted among wicked people.
If he adds foolishness to his sins, it is punished among us, and he will present his words before God.
Elihu answered and said:
Did you consider this just when you said, 'I am more righteous than God'?
If you say, “What benefit do you bring to yourself, and what profit is there in my condemning you?”
I will answer you and your friends with you.
Look at the heavens and consider the clouds, which are higher than you.
If you sin, what do you do to him? If your wickedness increases, what will you do to him?
If you are righteous, what benefit do you bring him, or what does he receive from you?
Your wickedness affects yourself, and your righteousness affects yourself.
They wail because of the abundance of oppression, and many cry out because of injustice.
And they did not say, “Where is God, who made us, who gives thought in the night?”
He has made us wiser than the animals of the earth and the birds of the sky.
There they cry out, but he does not answer them because of the pride of the wicked.
God does not listen in vain, nor does God praise him.
Even if you say you will not praise him, plead your case before him and implore him.
For now his anger does not punish, and he does not harm a person.
And Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.
Then Elihu continued and said:
“Wait for me a little, and I will show you, for there is still more to say on God's behalf.
I will bring my knowledge from far away and attribute righteousness to my Maker.
But truly my words are false, and my knowledge with you is without fault.
Look, God is mighty; he does not reject someone who is pure like milk.
The unjust person does not live, and he gives judgment to the wicked.
For the righteous person does not pass out of his sight. He seats kings on the throne, and they are exalted forever.
And if they are bound in chains and brought down in bonds to poverty,
he will show them their deeds and their offenses, because they have acted arrogantly.
He will open their ears to correction and tell them to turn back from injustice.
They will listen and obey, and they will spend their days in prosperity and their years in delight.
But if they do not listen, they will go to destruction and perish without knowledge.
The perverse in heart will perish, and they will not cry out; in anger they will cry out when he binds them.
Their souls will die in youth, and their lives will end in famine.
The humble person will be delivered through his humility, and he will reveal their way through affliction.
He will also deliver you from the mouth of the oppressor, giving you room instead of distress, and he will prepare a table full of rich food.
He will judge the wicked fully, bringing them to judgment, and they will be held by judgment.
He will not entice you with the fury of battle, nor will he require a great ransom from you.
He will prevail over you to deliver you, so that you need not be distressed by any of the mighty,
or by the oppression of the night. He will give peoples in exchange for you, and nations in exchange for your life.
Be careful not to turn toward injustice, for it is because of this that you have been tested through poverty.
God gives strength through his power. Who is a teacher like him?”
Who has given orders concerning his ways, and who has said to him, “You have done wrong”?
Remember that his works are many, and all people have praised him.
Human beings have seen him and gazed at him from afar.
Look, God is mighty and cannot be understood; there is no end to the counting of his years.
If he counts the pillars of heaven and forms the drops of rain by himself,
Which the heavens send down in season; the clouds shower it on people, and they rejoice greatly.
who can understand how he spreads the clouds from the abundance of his shelter?
He spreads his light above them and covers the depths of the sea.
For through these he judges the nations and gives food to many.
He covers the light with his hands and commands them to meet it.
He shows his possessions to his friends, and also to the wicked.
At this too his heart trembles and shakes from its place.
Listen carefully to his voice, to the angry judgment that comes from his mouth.
Under all the heavens they praise him, and his light reaches the ends of the earth.
After it he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not pursue them, so that they may hear his voice.
God thunders with his voice; he does wonders and great things and cannot be understood.
For he says to the snow, 'Become earth,' and to the rain and the heavy showers.
He has placed a seal on everyone's hand, to make everyone know his works.
The wild animal enters its hiding place and settles in its den.
From the chambers comes the whirlwind, and from the piercing wind comes frost.
By the breath of God ice is formed, and the abundance of water is diminished.
The clouds are gently stretched out, and he spreads the clouds of his light.
It circles and turns to carry out plans—everything he commands them over the face of his inhabited earth.
Whether for rulers, or for the earth, or for the devout person found in it.
Pay attention to this, Job; listen and consider God's wonders.
Look, do you know what God has laid upon them, and how he reveals the light of his clouds?
Do you know how the clouds go out, and the wonders of the one whose knowledge is flawless?
Your clothes grow warm, and the earth grows still because of the south wind.
Can you spread out the strong firmament with him and support it together?
Tell me what I should say to him, and let us not hide because of the darkness.
Shall I tell him what I would say? If a man speaks, he will be swallowed up.
Now they do not see the light, though it is bright in the expanse of heaven; the wind passes through and clears the skies.
Gold comes from the north, and mighty light comes from God.
He is mighty in power and judgment and great in righteousness; he does not oppress.
Therefore people fear him, and all who are wise in heart tremble before him.
The Lord answered Job from the whirlwind and said:
Who is this who devises counsel with words without knowledge?
Now brace yourself like a warrior. I will question you, and you must tell me.
Where were you when I was establishing the earth’s foundations? Tell me, if you have understanding.
Who determined its measurements, if you know? Who stretched a measuring line over it?
On what do its sides stand? Or who laid stones at its corners?
He created the morning stars together, and all the sons of the angels shouted for joy.
He shut the gates of the sea, made it burst out from the womb, and brought it out.
When he set the cloud as its clothing and made thick darkness its wrapping,
he established a covenant for it and made gates and bars.
I said, ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here you must stop in the pride of your waves.’
Have you ever in your lifetime commanded the morning? Do you know where dawn’s place is,
so that it may take hold of the earth’s edges and the wicked may be shaken out of it?
Their bodies will be changed like clay, and they will stand like a garment.
Their light will be withheld from sinners, and the uplifted arm will be broken.
Have you entered the depths of the sea and walked among the foundations of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you, and the gates of the shadows of death?
Have you seen the whole breadth of the earth? Tell me, if you know.
By what road does light dwell, and where is the place of darkness,
if you know its boundary and the path to its house?
And do you know when you were born, and whether the number of your days is great?
Have you entered the storehouses of snow, and have you seen the storehouses of hail,
which are kept for a time of distress and for a day of battle and war?
Or by which path is light divided, and does the wind go out over the earth?
And there is a sight and a sound.
To bring rain down on a land without people, and in a wilderness where no human being lives,
to satisfy every forest and make shoots of [?] spring up.
Does the rain have a father, or who fathered the drops?
And the dew and ice—from whose womb did they come out? And who gave birth to the frost of heaven?
The waters harden like stones, and the surfaces of the depths freeze solid.
Can you hold back the Pleiades, or have you seen the path of Orion?
Look, can you bring out the Wagon in its season, or do you stand before the Bear?
Do you know the law of heaven, or do you establish its law on earth?
